sentences.text: Blade inspection is initiated when scheduled surveillance, turbine alarms, or operational reports indicate that blade condition requires review.
The Maintenance Planning Engine combines inspection intervals, prior defect history, and turbine availability to propose survey dates.
The Duty Planner confirms the inspection priority and coordinates access with the Marine Coordinator or the Field Supervisor.
The Weather Service and Metocean Buoy provide forecasts and measured conditions for assessing whether remote or close-access work is safe.
Remote surveys use the Blade Inspection Drone to capture repeatable views of blade surfaces while the turbine is in an approved operating state.
The Blade Specialist reviews the tile image to classify visible damage and identify areas requiring closer assessment.
Image records are linked to the turbine, blade, inspection date, viewing angle, and relevant operating conditions.
The SCADA Gateway provides operating data that helps distinguish persistent defects from transient changes in blade appearance.
The Shore Control Room monitors turbine status and records any operating restrictions required during the remote survey.
A remote finding that is uncertain, growing, or potentially safety significant is referred for close-access inspection.
Close-access work is planned only after the responsible team verifies turbine isolation, rotor restraint, access arrangements, and rescue provisions.
The HSE Officer reviews the work method, exposure controls, and emergency arrangements before personnel approach the rotor.
The Blade Specialist examines the affected surface using suitable lighting, measurement tools, and nondestructive inspection methods.
Defect records describe location, dimensions, orientation, suspected cause, confidence, and any change from earlier observations.
Cracks, erosion, coating loss, lightning damage, bond-line indications, and drainage concerns are assessed against approved engineering criteria.
The Blade Specialist distinguishes cosmetic damage from conditions that could affect structural integrity or safe turbine operation.
When evidence is incomplete, the inspection record identifies the uncertainty and specifies additional measurements or imagery needed.
The Field Supervisor confirms that close-access findings are documented before personnel leave the work area.
The Maintenance Planning Engine uses the assessed severity, defect growth rate, weather exposure, and production impact to support repair prioritization.
The Duty Planner assigns a target repair window and coordinates required personnel, equipment, and vessel capacity.
The Storekeeper checks repair materials and tooling against the approved repair method before mobilization.
The Service Operations Vessel prepares the Recovery Basket Load Sheet for the planned work activity.
Repair plans identify surface preparation, material application, cure requirements, inspection hold points, and acceptance criteria.
After repair, the Blade Specialist records the completed work and verifies that the repaired area meets the applicable acceptance criteria.
The Duty Planner updates the maintenance record and schedules follow-up inspection when residual uncertainty or defect history warrants it.
